summary: First-iteration full-stack test of KinoKontroll (Norwegian video-wall app). Backend: 17/17 pytest tests pass (auth, state, video upload/list/stream/range/delete, WebSocket initial state + unauthorized rejection + authorized play/pause/volume/loop broadcasts). Frontend: landing shows 3 nav cards, /control & /upload correctly redirect to /login when no token, wrong password shows Norwegian error toast, correct password 'kino123' navigates to /control, all control transport/volume/timeline/connection-status testids render, /upload dropzone accepts a small .mp4 and the clip appears in list, /display renders idle placeholder and video element. Real-time WebSocket connects (brief 'closed before established' warning during initial handshake is cosmetic — reconnect hook immediately resyncs).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py streams videos by loading ENTIRE object bytes into memory on every request (get_object reads resp.content then slices for Range). For anything beyond small clips this will blow memory and make seeking slow. Recommend passing Range through to object storage or caching bytes in a disk/stream buffer.
Storage client is synchronous (requests.post/get/put) inside async endpoints — each upload/stream blocks the event loop. Wrap in asyncio.to_thread or use httpx.AsyncClient.
@app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') is deprecated in modern FastAPI — prefer lifespan context managers.

WebSocket token is sent inside every message payload in plain JSON. OK for a single shared password but document that clearly; consider accepting a one-time auth frame then marking the socket as authenticated instead of re-verifying each action (minor perf).
Upload endpoint reads full file into memory (await file.read()) — for large videos this will OOM. Stream to storage instead.
No file size cap on /api/videos/upload — add a max-size guard to prevent abuse.
CORS is wide-open ('*') with allow_credentials=True which browsers reject; not a bug today but tighten when deploying.
VideoOut.size relies on storage response 'size' key — if the storage API omits it the fallback is correct; keep the current len(data) fallback.
Frontend useSync.js ignores the 'error' message type — unauthorized WS commands are silently dropped. Surface via toast for better UX.
Display page passively trusts state.current_time for seek which may drift; current time_update loop from display is fine but could debounce more aggressively (every 500ms).
test_credentials: App password 'kino123' (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md). JWT returned from POST /api/auth/login stored in localStorage as 'kinokontroll_token'.
seed_data_creation: Backend tests upload and then soft-delete a TEST_clip.mp4 (4KB ftyp-prefixed bytes) per run — cleans itself up. Frontend test also uploaded one clip; clip may remain in DB under a tmp*.mp4 filename (small, 3.9 KB). Safe to keep or the main agent can delete via /upload UI.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest file is at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — run with: cd /app/backend && pytest tests/ -v --asyncio-mode=auto. Requires websockets + pytest-asyncio (both installed). All 17 tests passed on first run. Frontend app is Norwegian; expect toast text 'Feil passord' / 'Tilgang innvilget'. data-testids for all interactive elements are present. WebSocket endpoint at wss://<host>/api/ws — initial frame is {type:'state', state:{...}}, unauthorized commands respond with {type:'error', error:'unauthorized'}. /display is PUBLIC (no auth), /control and /upload are ProtectedRoute. Fake mp4 bytes are enough for backend upload/stream/range tests but will NOT play in the browser — use a real tiny mp4 if visual playback verification is needed.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — first iteration, no regressions found.
